title: Air-Fryer Pork Chops
subtitle: Juicy pork chops with a mustard and honey glaze from the air fryer
excerpt: Bone-in pork chops brushed with English mustard and honey, cooked in the air fryer until golden outside and just cooked through. On the table in 15 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pork chops benefit from the air fryer because the circulating hot air sears the outside quickly while keeping the inside moist. Bone-in chops are more forgiving than boneless: the bone conducts heat into the thickest part and the fat around the edge bastes the meat as it renders. The mustard and honey glaze adds flavour and helps the outside colour. Remove from the heat the moment the juices run clear.

recipeTools.notes: Any air fryer large enough to hold 2 chops flat.

content.text: Score the fat on the edge of each chop every 2 cm to prevent it curling up during cooking. The chops are done when the thickest part reads 63 C on a probe thermometer, or when the juices run clear. Rest for 3 minutes: the temperature will rise a further 2 to 3 degrees and the juices will redistribute.

Preheat the air fryer to 200 C for 3 minutes. Score the fat on the edge of each chop. Mix the mustard, honey, olive oil, garlic powder, salt, and pepper together. Brush the mixture over both sides of each chop.
Place the chops in the air fryer basket. Cook at 200 C for 6 minutes. Flip and cook for a further 5 to 6 minutes until the outside is golden and the juices run clear.
Rest on a warm plate for 3 minutes before serving.
